adjara-english-essay-competition-grade-1.about:
The Adjara Ministry of Education and Sport's essay competition is open to 10th-grade pupils of public and private schools in Adjara. It is held in English over three rounds: the first two are written essays, and the third is a presentation and interview.

It builds exactly the skills needed for scholarship and university applications abroad: academic writing in English, argument and speaking under pressure.
highlights: Written in English: great practice for applications abroad
Final round with presentation and interview
Open to public and private schools
adjara-english-essay-competition-grade-1.eligibility: Grade X pupils of public and private schools in the Autonomous Republic of Adjara. Good English required.
how_to_apply: Watch the ministry's olympiads & competitions page for the 2027 regulation
Register as the regulation describes
Write the two essay rounds
If selected, present and answer questions in the final

adjara-eurodyssey-internship-abroad.about:
Since 2006 the Adjara Ministry of Education and Sport has run Georgia's entry into Eurodyssey, the youth exchange programme of the Assembly of European Regions (founded 1985). Participants complete a professional internship in a member region in Europe to build work skills and language ability.

Internships last several months depending on the host region and are fully funded by the host: a monthly stipend of 700-1,200 EUR covers food and accommodation, and the internship starts with an intensive language course and a cultural programme. AER co-funds insurance; the intern pays travel and visa costs, and after completion the Adjara ministry pays a one-off 2,000 GEL.

Selection has two stages: the ministry's own competition, then registration on eurodyssey.aer.eu and a remote interview with the host region and employer, who make the final decision.
highlights: Monthly stipend of 700-1,200 EUR paid by the host region
Free intensive language course in the host country
Extra 2,000 GEL from the Adjara ministry after completion
adjara-eurodyssey-internship-abroad.eligibility: Citizens of Georgia aged 18-35 registered in the Autonomous Republic of Adjara, with a vocational or higher education diploma and knowledge of a foreign language, who meet the host region's requirements.
how_to_apply: Read the regulation and document list on the ministry's "Internship abroad" page
Submit the application form and documents to the ministry during the announced registration period
Pass the ministry's first-stage selection
Register your profile on eurodyssey.aer.eu
Interview remotely with the host region and employer
adjara-eurodyssey-internship-abroad.costs: Host region pays a 700-1,200 EUR monthly stipend and language course; travel and visa paid by the intern; 2,000 GEL one-off support from Adjara after completion.

adjara-literary-marathon-2027.about:
The Literary Marathon is part of the Adjara Ministry of Education and Sport's annual olympiads and competitions. Pupils compete in two categories: grades VII-VIII and grades IX-X.

The first round is organised by the ministry and the regional education resource centres; the second is a live written face-off with a host. It suits keen readers who want to test their knowledge of Georgian and world literature.
highlights: For keen readers in two age groups
Live final with a host
Run every year by the regional ministry
adjara-literary-marathon-2027.eligibility: Pupils in grades VII-X of schools in the Autonomous Republic of Adjara.
how_to_apply: Check the 2027 regulation on the ministry's page
Register through your school or resource centre
Take the first round
Compete in the live final if selected

adjara-school-fine-arts-competition-2027.about:
The Adjara Ministry of Education and Sport's fine arts competition invites pupils to create a themed painting. Categories: grades 5-7 and grades 8-10.

The theme and rules are set in the annual regulation published on the ministry's olympiads & competitions page.
highlights: Two age categories
Themed painting competition
Free, run annually by the ministry
adjara-school-fine-arts-competition-2027.eligibility: Pupils in grades V-X of schools in the Autonomous Republic of Adjara.
how_to_apply: Read the 2027 regulation for the theme
Create your painting
Submit it as instructed by the ministry

adjara-school-team-competition-2027.about:
Alongside its olympiad, the Adjara Ministry of Education and Sport holds a team competition for primary and lower-secondary pupils. Each school can enter one team of five pupils from grades 5-6 and one from grades 7-9 in Georgian language and literature and in mathematics; history and civic education (integrated) is for grades 7-9 teams.

It rewards teamwork and broad knowledge and is a friendly first competition for younger students.
highlights: Teams of five represent their school
Maths, Georgian, history and civics
Great first competition for younger pupils
adjara-school-team-competition-2027.eligibility: Teams of five pupils (grades 5-6 or 7-9) nominated by general education schools in Adjara.
how_to_apply: Ask your school to nominate a team when the 2027 regulation is published
Prepare with the published past tests
Compete on the announced date

adjara-subject-olympiad-2027.about:
The Adjara Ministry of Education and Sport runs a subject olympiad every year under its 'Competitions and Olympiads' subprogramme. Subjects: Georgian language and literature, English and mathematics (grades VII-IX), plus physics, chemistry and biology (grade IX). For Russian-sector pupils, physics, maths, chemistry and biology are held in Russian.

The olympiad is a written test. It is a good warm-up for the national school olympiad and for international olympiads, and past tests are published on the ministry's page.
highlights: Six subjects from languages to sciences
Past tests published for practice
Stepping stone to national olympiads
adjara-subject-olympiad-2027.eligibility: Pupils in grades VII-IX of schools in the Autonomous Republic of Adjara (physics, chemistry and biology: grade IX only).
how_to_apply: Check the ministry's olympiads & competitions page from February 2027
Register through your school as set out in the regulation
Practise with the published past tests
Sit the test on the announced date

agricultural-university-georgia-grants-2.about:
The Agricultural University of Georgia (AUG) in Tbilisi, a private university known for agriculture, engineering, natural sciences and its strong maths and physics programmes, publishes a tuition table by state-grant level and several funding options for each admission year.

For 2026 admission these included: the Bank of Georgia scholarship for students (stipendia.bog.ge); 'Sagzuri' for socially vulnerable students admitted through the national exams; the study grant 'Best to the Best' (saukeTeso – saukeTesoebs) for top entrants; and knowledge competitions held during the year that give applicants an extra chance to win study grants. AUG shares the campus and funding philosophy of Free University (Kakha Bendukidze).
highlights: Merit grant 'Best to the Best' for top entrants
'Sagzuri' grant for socially vulnerable students
Competitions during the year to win study grants
agricultural-university-georgia-grants-2.eligibility: Applicants admitted to AUG bachelor's programmes through the 2027 Unified National Exams; Sagzuri requires official socially vulnerable status; competition grants for participants in AUG's knowledge competitions.
how_to_apply: Check AUG's financing page for the 2027 package.
Take part in AUG's knowledge competitions during the school year (extra grant chance).
Sit the 2027 UNE and choose an AUG programme.
Apply for the Bank of Georgia scholarship via stipendia.bog.ge if eligible.
agricultural-university-georgia-grants-2.costs: Tuition reductions or full coverage depending on the grant; tuition depends on the state-grant level.

alte-university-funding-2027.about:
Alte University in Tbilisi runs a broad merit funding scheme for UNE entrants: 100% funding for any applicant in the national UNE top 1,000 who chooses Alte first; 50% for school gold and silver medallists who choose Alte first; 100% for the top 10 entrants to the medicine programme, paid by the company VIAN; 100% for national olympiad winners entering computer science, artificial intelligence or business administration; and 100% for entrants to business, computer science and AI who score at least 60% of the maximum in the elective subject (physics or mathematics).

The last rule makes Alte one of the most accessible fully funded options in Georgia for strong maths/physics students.
highlights: 100% for national top 1,000, olympiad winners and top 10 in medicine
100% for business/CS/AI entrants with ≥60% in maths or physics
50% for gold/silver medallists
alte-university-funding-2027.eligibility: Applicants entering Alte University bachelor's programmes via the 2027 Unified National Exams (first priority for the top-1,000 and medal grants).
how_to_apply: Register for the 2027 Unified National Exams.
Choose Alte University first (and the relevant programme: medicine, CS, AI or business).
Achieve the qualifying rank/score or present your olympiad diploma or medal.
Funding is applied on enrolment under Alte's funding rules document.
alte-university-funding-2027.costs: 100% or 50% of tuition depending on the scheme.

american-corner-akhaltsikhe-georgia.about:
American Corner Akhaltsikhe is part of the U.S. Embassy in Georgia's network of 20 American Spaces, run in partnership with local libraries (Akhaltsikhe Central Library, 6a Tamar Mephe Street). Corners host English conversation clubs, science and theme clubs, talks by American diplomats and guest speakers on topics such as entrepreneurship and women's empowerment, and offer English-learning materials and computers to learn about the United States.

Activities are free and open to the public; most participants are school and university students. It is also a practical place to hear about U.S. exchange programmes (such as FLEX), EducationUSA advising and other embassy opportunities, and to network with peers for your own projects.

There is no application round: follow the Corner's page for the weekly schedule and sign-up links for individual events.
highlights: Free English conversation and science clubs
Meet American diplomats and visiting speakers
Hear first about U.S. exchanges and embassy programmes
american-corner-akhaltsikhe-georgia.eligibility: Open to everyone; activities are mostly aimed at school and university students. Some clubs are grouped by English level or age.
how_to_apply: Visit the Corner at Akhaltsikhe Central Library, 6a Tamar Mephe Street or follow its official page
Check the weekly schedule of clubs and events
Register for the activity you want (some events ask for sign-up in advance)

american-councils-erlp-georgian-tbilisi-.about:
American Councils for International Education runs the Eurasian Regional Language Program (ERLP) in Tbilisi, an immersive Georgian-language programme taught by native-speaker experts at the American Councils Language Center in Vake. Classes (about 15 contact hours a week) cover phonetics, grammar, conversation, reading and composition, plus topics in Georgian literature, history, politics and media; heritage speakers and complete beginners are both catered for.

Participants live with Georgian host families (private room, two meals a day), meet regular conversation partners, join weekly cultural activities and regional excursions, and can add internships or volunteering. Academic credit is issued through Bryn Mawr College. The programme is self-funded, with financial aid available, and is aimed mainly at students from the United States, but the page sets no citizenship limit beyond being 18+.

The fall 2027 semester runs 24 August – 11 December 2027 (US$16,400) and the academic year runs to 14 May 2028 (US$29,900). Semester students earn 16 undergraduate or 15 graduate credits and can request split programming with Russian. ERLP generally expects two semesters of prior study of the target or a related language. Apply by 15 March 2027.
highlights: Full immersion: classes, homestay, conversation partners
Optional internships or volunteering in Tbilisi
Academic credit through Bryn Mawr College
american-councils-erlp-georgian-tbilisi-.eligibility: Undergraduates, graduates and professionals aged 18+; ERLP normally requires about two semesters of prior study of Georgian or a related language for semester/year options.
how_to_apply: Choose Fall 2027 or Academic Year 2027–28 on the programme page
Complete the online application ($45 fee) by 15 March 2027
Accepted students confirm with a $1,000 deposit
american-councils-erlp-georgian-tbilisi-.costs: Semester US$16,400; academic year US$29,900 (tuition, homestay with two meals a day, excursions, insurance). Financial aid available; flights not included.

Summer participants can study Georgian, Armenian, Azerbaijani or Russian with no prior study required, and earn 8 undergraduate or 10 graduate credits. Apply by 15 February 2027.
highlights: Homestay with a Georgian family and weekly excursions
Beginner to advanced levels; credit via Bryn Mawr College
Financial aid available
american-councils-erlp-georgian-tbilisi-.eligibility: Undergraduates, graduates and professionals aged 18+ by the deadline. Summer: no prior language study required for the regional-language option.
how_to_apply: Open the Georgian programme page on American Councils Study Abroad
Create an account and complete the online application ($45 fee, waivable for low-income students)
Submit by 15 February 2027
Accepted students pay a $1,000 deposit within two weeks
american-councils-erlp-georgian-tbilisi-.costs: US$7,400 for summer 2027 (tuition, housing with meals, excursions, insurance); $45 application fee. Financial aid available; flights not included.

batumi-youth-initiatives-support-2026.about:
Under its Youth Centre sub-programme, Batumi City Hall funds events designed and led by young people themselves. Eligible themes include education and culture, sport and healthy lifestyles, youth policy, hiking, cycling and water-sports tourism, educational excursions, exhibitions of crafts, career guidance, young scientists, ecology and environmental protection, and civic engagement. Each project can receive up to 4,000 GEL (taxes included).

Projects must be participatory events (not equipment purchases or websites), held in Batumi during the budget year, ideally at least 22 days after the monthly application window closes. A commission scores relevance, duration (longer projects score higher) and the applicant's capacity to deliver, and may interview you or ask for a 5-minute presentation. There is no fixed number of winners until the annual budget runs out.

A practical way for school and university students in Batumi to fund a club, festival, workshop or volunteering campaign and gain project-management experience.
highlights: Up to 4,000 GEL for your own youth project
Open from age 14 (minors apply with a parent)
Monthly decisions; no limit on number of winners until the budget is used
batumi-youth-initiatives-support-2026.eligibility: Individuals aged 14-29 registered as residents of Batumi municipality. Applicants under 18 apply through a legal guardian. Documents must be in Georgian.
how_to_apply: Download the regulation and application form (Annex 2) from the programme page on batumi.gov.ge
Prepare the application, CV, recommendation letter, ID copy, proof of Batumi registration (or civil registry screenshot), bank details and, for items over 500 GEL, two price quotes
Submit at Batumi City Hall's records office, 25 Luka Asatiani Street, during any month's window
Present your project to the commission (in person or by phone) if invited
If funded, sign the contract, run the event and submit programme and financial reports within 15 days
batumi-youth-initiatives-support-2026.costs: Free to apply. Grant of up to 4,000 GEL paid against documented expenses; costs before the contract are not reimbursed.

batumi-youth-international-projects-supp.about:
This Batumi City Hall programme (sub-programme 'Support for Professional Development') helps young people from Batumi take up opportunities abroad: professional internships, practical placements and retraining, as well as educational, cultural, sports, youth, volunteering and other international projects, trainings and courses. It works as co-funding: you already hold an invitation and some funding, and the city adds up to 3,000 GEL.

Applications are accepted every month, from the first to the last working day. A commission reviews the file and interviews applicants within ten working days after the month closes; you need at least 60% of the maximum score to be recommended, and the mayor's order confirms the grant. Costs incurred before the contract is signed are not reimbursed, so apply well before you travel. After the trip you submit a short report and copies of passport stamps.

Useful for Batumi students accepted to Erasmus+ youth exchanges, summer schools, conferences or internships whose costs are not fully covered.
highlights: Up to 3,000 GEL per person for travel, visa, insurance and fees
Monthly intake all year; decision within about 10 working days
Covers internships, trainings, exchanges, volunteering and sports or cultural projects abroad
batumi-youth-international-projects-supp.eligibility: Citizens of Georgia aged 18-29 registered as residents of Batumi municipality, who hold higher or vocational education or are currently enrolled at an authorised university or vocational college, and have a written invitation to the project abroad. Documents in Georgian (foreign-language documents need a notarised translation).
how_to_apply: Download the regulation, application form (Annex 2) and recommendation form (Annex 4) from the programme page on batumi.gov.ge
Collect: ID/passport copy, proof of Batumi registration, recommendation letter, invitation, two 3x4 photos, proof of co-funding (bank statement or sponsor letter) and proof of study or education
Submit the file at Batumi City Hall's records office, 25 Luka Asatiani Street, between 09:00 and 18:00 during the month
Attend the commission interview; if approved, sign the contract with the City Hall before travelling
Within two months after the project, submit the programme report (Annex 5) and passport stamp copies
batumi-youth-international-projects-supp.costs: Free to apply. One-off grant of up to 3,000 GEL covering travel, visa, insurance, registration or participation fees; the applicant must show co-funding for the rest.

bsu-batumi-scholarships-2027.about:
Batumi Shota Rustaveli State University, the main public university of the Adjara region on the Black Sea coast, runs several scholarship lines: university named scholarships for top bachelor's and master's students with research achievements; awards for excellent and socially vulnerable students from the second year; a scholarship for first-year students who list BSU first in the Unified National Exams and achieve high results; and sponsor scholarships from the Bank of Georgia, the Gudavadze-Patarkatsishvili Foundation and the Tamaz Bekaia Foundation.

Socially vulnerable high-achieving students can also receive tuition support from the university budget on a competitive basis.
highlights: Bank of Georgia and private foundation scholarships
Award for first-year students who choose BSU first
Support for socially vulnerable high achievers
bsu-batumi-scholarships-2027.eligibility: Students enrolled at BSU (some awards for first-year entrants via UNE who rank BSU first; others from the second year, based on grades, research and social status).
how_to_apply: Choose BSU as first priority in the Unified National Exams (for the first-year award).
Watch BSU's scholarships page for competitions each semester.
Submit the application with transcript and, where relevant, social-status documents.
bsu-batumi-scholarships-2027.costs: Monthly stipends or tuition support depending on the scholarship.

caucasus-university-applicant-info-meeti.about:
Caucasus University (CU), a private university in Tbilisi known for business, law, media and computer science, is holding an information meeting for applicants on 12 November 2026 at 14:00 (check-in from 13:30) on its campus.

Applicants meet the deans of CU's schools, hear about the bachelor's programmes and the opportunities the university offers, and take part in a Q&A. Registration through the link on the event page is required.

Useful for final-year pupils comparing Tbilisi universities before the national exams.
highlights: Meet CU's deans in person
Overview of all bachelor's programmes
Q&A for applicants
caucasus-university-applicant-info-meeti.eligibility: Prospective bachelor's applicants (mainly grades 11-12) and their parents. Georgian-language.
how_to_apply: Open the event page on cu.edu.ge
Register through the linked form
Arrive at the CU campus by 13:30 on 12 November 2026

caucasus-university-top-501-cu-grant-202.about:
Caucasus University (CU), a private university in Tbilisi, runs two entrance funding schemes linked to the Unified National Exams. TOP 501: any applicant ranked among the 501 best UNE competitive scores nationwide studies free for the full programme (annual fee GEL 8,990 for most programmes). In 2025 this meant scores between 2,112 and 2,308.8. Since 2019, 112 students have studied free under TOP 501.

CU Grant: applicants who choose any CU bachelor's programme as first priority and score 2,000+ receive an internal grant of GEL 3,500, 3,000, 2,500, 1,700 or 1,500 per year for the whole programme, on top of any state grant. CU also gives 100%, 50% and 30% funding to the top three students of each year in every school. Neither scheme applies to joint programmes with partner universities.
highlights: Full free tuition for national top 501 UNE scorers
GEL 1,500–3,500/year CU Grant for 2,000+ scores
Combinable with the Georgian state grant
caucasus-university-top-501-cu-grant-202.eligibility: Applicants entering a CU bachelor's programme through the 2027 Unified National Exams; TOP 501 requires a national top-501 competitive score; CU Grant requires 2,000+ points and CU as first priority. Not valid for joint programmes.
how_to_apply: Register for the Unified National Exams with NAEC in spring 2027.
Rank a Caucasus University bachelor's programme first in your choices.
Achieve a top-501 national score (full funding) or 2,000+ points (CU Grant).
The grant is applied automatically on enrolment; keep academic standing to retain it.

ejoi-georgia-team-selection-2027.about:
The European Junior Olympiad in Informatics (EJOI) is the main international programming olympiad for students under 16. Georgia's team is selected and trained by the Georgian Tech Olympiads Hub, run jointly by TBC Bank and BTU.

In the 2026 cycle, eligible pupils (born after 1 January 2011) registered through a Google form from 1 to 30 April, then sat two selection rounds on the BTU campus, each with three algorithmic problems in four hours. Four main members and two reserves were chosen and attended a 20-day training camp before EJOI 2026 in Kaunas, Lithuania (24-30 July). Expect the same timetable in 2027, with the birth-date cut-off moving one year.

A direct path to representing Georgia internationally, with free elite training for those selected.

Represent Georgia at EJOI

esc-climate-change-adaptation-zugdidi-20.about:
This volunteering opportunity is suited to someone interested in community engagement, climate resilience, and disaster preparedness. The volunteer will support local activities that help communities better understand environmental risks and improve preparedness for floods, extreme weather, and other climate-related challenges. Tasks may include helping organise workshops, discussions, awareness-raising events, and small community initiatives, as well as supporting communication with participants, preparing simple materials, and assisting with documentation and feedback collection. The volunteer will work closely with local communities, especially active residents and women, in a practical and people-centred environment. This is a meaningful opportunity to contribute to resilience-building while gaining hands-on experience in community work, local participation, and climate-related action.

Practical details: EU Humanitarian Aid volunteering (European Solidarity Corps) hosted by Merkuri in Zugdidi, Georgia; activity period 24 weeks within 4 January 2027 – 3 July 2027. Topics: development of disadvantaged areas, rural community development, climate change adaptation. The placement is open to residents of EU Member States, North Macedonia, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Türkiye (not Georgia). Deadline: 30 November 2026.

Living and learning: The volunteer will be accommodated in Zugdidi in a host family, in a private house with a separate individual room and access to shared facilities such as a kitchen, a bathroom, and a washing machine. A monthly subsistence allowance will be provided to cover food and personal expenses. Local transport costs will be reimbursed up to the agreed monthly limit. Visa fees, insurance, and one round-trip international ticket will be covered by the sending organisation. This opportunity is part of the RISE project (Reinforcing Inclusion through Solidarity and Empowerment), which offers volunteers the possibility to engage in local languages classes or intercultural activities, and benefit from three sides of mentoring (from the supporting organisation, the hosting… As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

esc-humanitarian-merkuri-youth-worker-zu.about:
Association Merkuri in Zugdidi is looking for a youth worker to lead programmes for children and young adults aged 8-25. The volunteer supports at-risk youth, raises awareness of domestic violence, facilitates workshops and discussions, develops clubs, social-education and creative projects with local young people, mentors local volunteers and contributes to monitoring and evaluation.

The placement runs from 4 January to 3 July 2027 within the BRIDGE project (Building Resilience, Innovation, Development and Gender Equality), which includes skills workshops, digital-literacy training and participation in UN Women events. The volunteer lives with a host family in a private room and receives a monthly allowance; travel, visa and insurance are covered.

esc-youth-worker-zugdidi-2027.about:
Are you passionate about empowering young people and making a real difference in their lives? Join Association Merkuri in Zugdidi, Georgia, to lead dynamic youth programs that actively engage children and young adults aged 8 to 25. In this role, you will provide vital support to at-risk youth, raise awareness about domestic violence, and facilitate impactful workshops and discussions tailored to their unique needs. eu-undp-young-content-creators-waste-cam.about:
Under the EU-funded project 'Circular Economy: Waste Reduction and Recycling for Citizens' Health', UNDP and the European Union invite young bloggers, vloggers and social-media creators from across Georgia to design and run campaigns on waste reduction, battery and e-waste recycling, packaging and sorting, reuse and repair, and responsible consumption.

Up to 12 participants will be selected. Between January and March 2027 they take part in training and mentoring, then create and publish the agreed content on their own TikTok, YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, X or other channels. Each receives a GEL 3,000 implementation award. Creativity and understanding of your audience matter more than follower count.

It is open to residents of Georgia aged 18-29, with young women and men from all regions and from under-served communities particularly encouraged. It is a paid, portfolio-building project for anyone interested in environmental communication or digital media.

Training and mentoring from UNDP's EU-funded project
No minimum follower count

flex-global-georgia-2028-29.about:
FLEX Global is the U.S. Department of State's merit-based high-school exchange that merges the Future Leaders Exchange (FLEX, 30+ years) and the Kennedy-Lugar Youth Exchange and Study (YES). It is implemented by American Councils for International Education with AFS, Amideast and iEARN, and Georgia is one of its 31 countries. Finalists spend a full year with a screened volunteer host family, attend a U.S. high school, do community service and take part in 'American Excellence' activities on business, technology and entrepreneurship.

The 2027-28 round for Georgia closed on 2026-10-22 (eligible then: grades 9, 10 or 11, born 1 Jan 2010 - 31 Dec 2011). FLEX has recruited every autumn for decades, so the 2028-29 round is expected to open around August-September 2027 with an October deadline and a birth window roughly one year later; the national office (https://georgia.americancouncils.org/) publishes the exact dates. Selection is free: English test, proctored essays, interview and a full application, with final selection in the U.S.

Use the year to prepare: keep grades high, practise English and short essays, and be ready to explain why you would be a good cultural ambassador. Finalists learn their status in spring and fly to the U.S. in August.
highlights: Full school year in the U.S. with a host family, fully funded
Merged FLEX + YES programme of the U.S. State Department, 31 countries
Free, merit-based selection: English test, essays, interview
flex-global-georgia-2028-29.eligibility: Citizens of Georgia enrolled in secondary school in Georgia: grades 9, 10 or 11, birth window for 2028-29 not yet published (2027-28 window was 1 Jan 2010 - 31 Dec 2011; expect it to move by about a year). Good academic standing, previous English study, U.S. J-1 visa eligibility and an international passport. Not eligible: students whose family has applied or plans to emigrate to the U.S.; usually not those who will have graduated before departure.
how_to_apply: Follow the Georgia FLEX Global office (https://georgia.americancouncils.org/) and the FLEX Global Instagram for the 2028-29 announcement (around September 2027)

Register on ais.americancouncils.org/flexglobal and take the English test

Submit the full application; finalists are announced in spring
flex-global-georgia-2028-29.costs: Free to apply. Not covered: passport costs, personal expenses beyond the stipend, excess baggage, internet/data plans.

Edison League (ედისონის ლიგა) is for pupils who like engineering, robotics, building things, programming and design, and who want to invent their own solutions rather than follow standard methods. It is run jointly by Free University of Tbilisi and the Agricultural University of Georgia.

Teams of up to three pupils from grades 10-12 (at least two must be final-year applicants) compete; teammates can come from different schools and solo registrants are helped to form teams. No prior preparation is needed. In 2026 the contest ran over 21-22 March at the Kakha Bendukidze Campus. The three best teams receive tuition grants of 15,000, 9,000 and 4,500 GEL (split between members) for engineering, physics, computer science, architecture or agricultural-science programmes at the two universities.

A practical, team-based engineering challenge with some of the largest school prizes in Georgia.

Lavoisier Circle (ლავუაზიეს წრე) is a team competition for pupils fascinated by biology, chemistry and the molecular make-up of living things, organised jointly by the Agricultural University of Georgia and Free University of Tbilisi.

Teams have up to three members, at least two of them final-year applicants; teammates can come from different schools, and individuals can register and be matched with a team. The top three teams win tuition grants of 15,000, 9,000 and 4,500 GEL (split equally between members) for bachelor's study in agronomy, natural sciences and biotechnology, veterinary medicine or engineering at the Agricultural University, or physics at Free University.

Generous prizes and a hands-on format make it one of the most rewarding school science contests in Georgia.

georgia-state-scholarships-for-students.about:
Georgia's Ministry of Education allocates each university a quota of state scholarships, which the university awards to its most successful students by academic performance. Tbilisi State University reported the scholarship as GEL 300 per month for one semester (GEL 1,500) in 2023-24, while Georgian Technical University's current page states GEL 150 per month; it is paid per semester and students can win it again in later semesters.

At Tbilisi State University 2,058 students received it in the autumn 2023-24 semester, so the odds are good for students with strong grades. Universities announce their own rules (GPA thresholds, credit load) and timelines.
highlights: Monthly state stipend for top students (GEL 150–300)
Thousands of awards nationwide
Renewable every semester
georgia-state-scholarships-for-students.eligibility: Bachelor's and master's students at Georgian universities that receive a quota, selected on academic performance under the university's rules.
how_to_apply: Keep a high GPA and full credit load.
Watch your university's scholarship/announcements page at the start of each semester.
Apply or be nominated as the university's rules require; recipients are confirmed by university order.
georgia-state-scholarships-for-students.costs: GEL 150–300 per month for one semester, depending on the university and year.

georgia-une-state-study-grant-2027.about:
Every school leaver who sits the Unified National Exams (UNE) in Georgia competes automatically for a state study grant. Grants are awarded on exam results and cover 50%, 70% or 100% of the standard annual state tuition of GEL 2,250 (for example, a 100% grant fully covers bachelor's tuition at Tbilisi State University). The grant follows the student to any accredited university, public or private; at private universities it is credited against the higher fee.

Registration takes place online with NAEC in spring, the exams are held in July, and grants are announced with the results in August. Many universities stack their own internal grants on top of the state grant for top scorers.

For Georgian students this is the single most important scholarship decision: good UNE preparation can make the whole degree free.
highlights: Up to 100% of GEL 2,250 annual tuition
Usable at any accredited Georgian university
Awarded automatically from UNE results; no separate application
georgia-une-state-study-grant-2027.eligibility: Graduates of general education (12th grade) in Georgia, or holders of an equivalent certificate, registering for the Unified National Exams. Georgian citizens and eligible residents; foreign nationals usually enter universities without UNE and are not eligible for the state grant.
how_to_apply: Register for the Unified National Exams on online.naec.ge during the spring registration window.
Choose the subjects required by your target programmes; sit the exams in July.
Rank your university/programme choices in the NAEC system.
Grant results are published with admission results; the grant is credited to your university each year you remain enrolled.
georgia-une-state-study-grant-2027.costs: State grant of 50%, 70% or 100% of GEL 2,250 per year. Any difference to a higher private-university fee is paid by the student or by internal grants.

georgian-american-university-top-grant-2.about:
Georgian American University, a private university in Tbilisi teaching business, law, international relations, computer science, AI, engineering and humanities, offers a TOP Grant: applicants whose overall UNE ranking places them in the national top 1,000 and who put GAU first study for free within the 240 credits of the bachelor's programme (retaking or extra courses are paid by the student).

GAU also awards the annual Sopo Shubladze university scholarship of GEL 5,000, and publishes programme-by-programme fees and co-funding options.
highlights: Free bachelor's for national top-1,000 UNE scorers
GEL 5,000 annual Sopo Shubladze scholarship
Programmes in business, law, IR, CS, AI and engineering
georgian-american-university-top-grant-2.eligibility: Applicants entering GAU bachelor's programmes through the 2027 Unified National Exams, ranked in the national top 1,000 and listing GAU first.
how_to_apply: Register for the 2027 Unified National Exams.
Choose a GAU bachelor's programme as your first priority.
Reach the national top 1,000; the TOP Grant is applied on enrolment.
Ask GAU about the Sopo Shubladze scholarship application once enrolled.
georgian-american-university-top-grant-2.costs: TOP Grant: 100% tuition for 240 credits. Sopo Shubladze scholarship: GEL 5,000 per year.

georgian-national-museum-volunteer-progr.about:
The Georgian National Museum, which unites Georgia's main museums (including the Simon Janashia Museum on Rustaveli Avenue), runs a volunteer programme to help people build professional skills in museum work. Volunteers name the department or unit they want to work in, so it suits students of history, archaeology, art, conservation, education or communications.

The museum looks for motivation, willingness to learn, a general understanding of the museum's work, responsibility and punctuality; computer skills and a foreign language are a plus. A recommendation from a school or workplace helps but is not required.

Apply by submitting the documents to the museum's administrative service; for questions call +995 32 299 80 22.
highlights: Hands-on experience in Georgia's leading museum
Choose the department you want to work in
Open year-round, any age
georgian-national-museum-volunteer-progr.eligibility: People of various ages with secondary or higher education and an interest in museum work. Foreign language skills are helpful for some projects.
how_to_apply: Prepare a volunteer application stating the department you want to join
Attach a recommendation (optional), CV, copy of diploma or school certificate, ID copy and two photos
Submit the documents to the museum's administrative service in Tbilisi
Wait to be contacted by the department (call +995 32 299 80 22 for updates)

gipa-zhvania-student-research-conference.about:
The Georgian Institute of Public Affairs (GIPA) holds an annual student research conference in memory of former Prime Minister Zurab Zhvania. The 2026 theme is 'Freedom as Responsibility', with three tracks: institution-building and Georgia's Euro-Atlantic course; from a strong state to a strong society (political dialogue and democratic leadership); and economic freedom and regional security, including energy independence and South Caucasus cooperation.

Bachelor's and master's students at any authorised Georgian higher-education institution can apply individually or in pairs by submitting a 300-500-word abstract (relevance and aim, methodology, key findings, conclusion, five keywords and a short bio) through GIPA's Google form between 26 October and 15 November 2026. Selected speakers are told on 20 November, submit final slides by 3 December and present for 10-15 minutes at GIPA, 22a Rustaveli Avenue, Tbilisi, on 9-10 December 2026. The working language is Georgian, but English presentations are welcome.

Participation is free; all speakers receive certificates, the best presenters win special prizes and strong papers may be published in the conference e-collection. A good first conference line for students in political science, IR, law or economics.
highlights: Open to students of any Georgian university
Prizes and possible publication for the best papers
English presentations accepted
gipa-zhvania-student-research-conference.eligibility: Bachelor's and master's students at authorised higher-education institutions in Georgia; individual or two-author submissions.
how_to_apply: Read the call on gipa.ge
Write a 300-500-word abstract with five keywords and a short bio
Submit it through GIPA's Google form by 15 November 2026
If selected (20 November), send final slides by 3 December
Present at GIPA on 9-10 December 2026

gita-electronics-world-arduino-zugdidi.about:
Electronics World (ელექტრონიკის სამყარო) is a five-day intensive at GITA's Zugdidi Technopark covering the basics of electronics and microcontrollers. Participants learn about electronic components, circuits and sensors, get started with the Arduino IDE and programming, and work with Arduino and ESP32 boards.

The course is for ages 13-15, is free, and ends with each participant building a mini-project. Registrants are called with the schedule.

It bridges the gap between toy kits and real embedded programming, useful for future robotics, IoT or engineering students.
highlights: Free, ages 13-15
Arduino IDE and ESP32 programming
Finish with your own mini-project
gita-electronics-world-arduino-zugdidi.eligibility: Ages 13-15; aimed at pupils in Zugdidi and Samegrelo. Georgian-language.
how_to_apply: Open the programme page on gita.gov.ge
Click through to the registration questionnaire on apps.mygita.ge and fill it in
Wait for GITA's call, SMS or email with the exact schedule
Attend the sessions at the technopark
